lawRefs: C.R.S. § 39-22-104(3) (add-back of federal deductions for AGI over $300,000)
Legislative Council Staff Economic & Revenue Forecast, September 2026 (State Controller TABOR certification of Sept 8 2026)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Values hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Rate: flat 4.40% of Colorado taxable income for 2026. The temporary TABOR rate reduction (C.R.S. 39-22-627) does NOT apply to tax year 2026: the State Controller certified on September 8, 2026 that FY 2025-26 revenue fell short of the Referendum C cap, so no TABOR refunds are made for tax year 2026 (LCS September 2026 forecast, https://content.leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/2026-09/sept2026-forecast-with-cover-for-remediation-and-posting-accessible.pdf). Starting point is federal taxable income, so the federal standard/itemized deduction is already embedded and standardDeduction is 0 here; there are no state personal exemptions. Taxpayers with federal AGI over $300,000 must add back federal standard/itemized deductions above $1,000 (single) / $2,000 (joint) for 2026 and later (the limits were $12,000 / $16,000 for 2023-2025) - not expressible in this schema. Pension/annuity subtraction (per person; for those under 65 the cap also covers taxable Social Security): $20,000 at age 55-64, $24,000 at age 65+; under 55 only for death benefits. Social Security: age 65+ subtract all federally taxable benefits; age 55-64 subtract all if AGI does not exceed $75,000 (single) / $95,000 (joint), otherwise the $20,000 cap applies; under 55 taxable (except death benefits). Other Colorado additions to federal taxable income are not modeled. No general capital-gains exclusion. Cross-checked against Tax Foundation, "State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026" (data as of Jan 1 2026, updated Feb 11 2026).

flags.taxesSocialSecurity: partial: 65+ fully exempt; 55-64 exempt if AGI <= $75,000 single / $95,000 joint, else combined $20,000 cap with pensions; under 55 taxable
